title: SHINE lights up the extremes
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02017-8

The Shanghai High Repetition Rate XFEL and Extreme Light Facility is approaching its first lasing. Nature Photonics spoke with Zhentang Zhao, director of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility and the SHINE project, about the facility’s capabilities and future plans.

title: Delaying light from quantum dots
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02015-w

Förster energy transfer can prolong the photoluminescence decay of a receiving colloidal quantum dot, revealing a possible route to optically control recombination in nanocrystal assemblies.

title: Time-stretch spectroscopy breaks temporal aliasing barrier
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02006-x

A temporally super-resolved single-shot method overcomes the long-standing temporal–spectral trade-off in time-stretch spectroscopy. The outcome is continuous measurements of non-repetitive spectral dynamics with picosecond resolution, providing a three-orders-of-magnitude improvement over the current state of the art.

title: One super sensor from many
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01994-0

By combining 48 parallel sensors with diffractive multiplexing to recover information from the gaps between the sensors, a new wide-field microscope achieves a spatial resolution of approximately 3 micrometres over more than 5.2 square centimetres at 120 frames per second, substantially relaxing the conventional trade-off between field of view, resolution and imaging speed.

title: Optomechanics for piconewton force metrology
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02011-0

Of the sensors that can directly sense forces in the pico- and sub-pico-newton ranges, only a few can measure in liquids. Microfibre-based microcantilevers now add to this family, providing a versatile, broad-bandwidth, high-sensitivity optomechanical sensor.

title: Hybrid nanophotonic trap boosts atomic storage and coherence times
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02005-y

A hybrid nanophotonic trap that replaces the attractive red-detuned laser field with atom–surface interactions — Casimir–Polder interactions and electrostatic attraction — achieves record-long storage and coherence times for cold atoms coupled to a nanofibre surface.

title: Microchip Nd:YAG laser with master-oscillator–power-amplifier architecture
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01984-2

This work reports an integrated Nd:Y3Al5O12 laser–amplifier system based on a microchip master-oscillator–power-amplifier architecture. A double-resonant microring seed with a 2.9 μW threshold is combined with waveguide amplifiers, enabling continuous-wave output powers exceeding 12 dBm.
